title: The stadium dance hall and the aftermath in Ankara
summary: Collier asks details: the stadium was turned into a dance hall to celebrate the execution; no one saw Atatürk, and the musicians were confined to hotels and returned.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well, now, let me ask you, there's a couple of things about this that I don't understand.
In other words, this was a big like a big dance pavillion, or something.
Where --
Where you were playing?
Yeh, yeh, now, Para?
Yes. No, no, when you were playing in -- for the execution.
Yes, it was what you would call a stadium. Some type of a stadium
Briggs
Right.
I mean a great big awning. A stadium with all commodities and everything.
Right.
You see.
Right.
And they transformed that into a dance hall, for that evening.
So they would dance and rejoice at the execution of the politicians.
Then the place was full of people, I guess.
Naturally, yes.
They were all standing there and waiting while the band --
They were all standing and waiting while the band --
And then as soon as the execution happened, then the band started up and they all started to dance?
Briggs
That's it.
Did Kemel Attaturk turn up.

I didn't see him. Yeh, but I didn't see him. We didn't see -- no one saw him. But he must have been there, because we were told after that he was the type of man, his eyes were -- what would you say, "cross-eyed", and he -- each eye was looking in a different direction, not cross-eyed, but --
I see, the other way.

Both eyes were looking in a different direction. (wall-eyed) They claimed he was an awful person to see. But the point is they had taken us back to the hotel the next morning, and we were nicely treated, had everything, all the refreshments and everything that we wanted, but fortunately for us, we didn't get
Briggs 167
to the marketplace, because we might have disappeared also.
Right, yes.
So we were very happy to get back to Para.
